title: Compute money in integer minor units with explicit rounding

facts.note: Role (PLT-84), mapped to paths by the structure profile.
The task computes or converts monetary amounts.
Diff adds or edits arithmetic on values that represent money.

fires: A rule multiplies an amount by a fractional rate or percentage.
A rule converts a non-monetary unit (credits, quantity, rate) into an amount.
A new amount field is added to a value returned at the boundary.
doesNotFire: Display-only formatting of an amount that is already computed.
Counting items or units that never become an amount.

given: A rule in the domain or application role computes, converts or returns a monetary amount
when: the agent writes or edits that arithmetic
then: Keep every amount an integer number of minor units, and round only at an explicitly chosen step with an explicit rounding mode.
prefer: Convert other units (rates, percentages, exchange or credit ratios) to minor units in one named step, then do integer arithmetic.
Name the rounding mode where it is applied; reuse the codebase's existing rounding helper if one exists.
State the unit in the name or type of each amount.
avoid: Binary floating amounts carried between steps and rounded only at the end.
Rounding the same value twice, or rounding at different steps on different code paths.
why: Amounts that drift by one minor unit break reconciliation, totals and audit, and the error is invisible in happy-path tests.
evidence: Every amount crossing a function boundary is an integer in minor units.
Each rounding site is explicit and covered by a test with a value that exercises it (a .5 case).
